value: Only statement 1: a perfectly competitive firm faces perfectly elastic demand
reasoning: A firm in perfect competition is a price taker and faces a horizontal, perfectly elastic demand curve. A monopolistically competitive firm faces a downward-sloping and fairly elastic demand curve because of close substitutes, not a perfectly inelastic one, so statement 2 is wrong.

value: The claim that a nation without absolute advantage cannot gain from trade is incorrect
reasoning: Ricardo's comparative advantage theory, set out in 'On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation' (1817), shows that both nations gain by specialising in the good with the lower opportunity cost. Its central point is that even a nation with no absolute advantage in any good can still benefit from trade, so statement C contradicts the theory.

value: Pitt's India Act: Board of Control; 1813: end of trade monopoly; 1833: no discrimination in employment; 1853: enlarged legislative council

This gives A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1.

value: The President shall act on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister

Options A and D describe Articles 53 and 85, and B is the Prime Minister's duty under Article 78, none of which the amendment changed.

value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the CAG does not control the issue of money
